summary: Re-review of the S2 remediation round 2 at f617412f. F7 is fixed: 35ffb32b replaces WHOLE_LINE_DISABLE_RE with BLOCK_COMMENT_RE plus BLOCK_DISABLE_RE, and both helpers now count and strip each block disable span in any position. I drove the exact helper code extracted from the test file through a direct node check with 26 edge assertions: mid-line block, multi-line block, both spellings, rule lists, '-- reason', the block spellings of disable-next-line and disable-line, the JSX-wrapped form, two spans on one line, and a non-disable block comment (prose and mid-line) that neither counts nor strips. All 26 pass. A live oxlint probe in an isolated worktree confirms the jsx-wrap-midline form: the original hides no-unused-vars with exit 0, the stripped copy surfaces it with exit 1. No case got weaker in 35ffb32b: the commit touches only the two helpers and their comments (32 insertions, 30 deletions, all helper lines); adv 1 to 9 are untouched and adv 9 passes as written. The fixture still matches the tree exactly: 49 carriers against 49 entries, zero unlisted, zero stale, zero kind, count, or blanket mismatches under the new counting, and the fixture file itself is unchanged. No tracked source file holds a true mid-line or multi-line disable (the two near hits are JSX-wrapped whole-line forms in pre-calculus that the fixture records). Every plan and log line added since 4326142c is true: the S2 remediation sub-box claims all re-verified (S2 adversarial 9 pass, S2 oxlint 7 pass, S1 adversarial 7 pass, S1 vinext 1.x 11 pass, npx tsc --noEmit exit 0, full scripts suite 57 passed 1 failed with only the pre-existing remediate-concept-blueprints row). Provenance: HEAD equaled f617412f at audit start; a parallel adversarial r3 run in this same checkout then committed f2e55c8c (adv 10 to 12) and d3822d47 (its result) after my HEAD, and its uncommitted working-tree edits contaminated my first full-suite run (61 tests, 4 failed). I therefore ran the full suite in a detached worktree at f617412f through heavy-run.sh: 58 tests, 57 passed, 1 failed (the known row only), exit 1, which matches the Green r6 log. My verdict is bound to f617412f per the brief. The adversarial r3 result (status fail, blocker F1r3: the sweep is blind for // disable forms on CRLF files; F2r3: an in-string /* breaks the sweep copy) owns the routing of the two new latent guard weaknesses I confirmed at my HEAD by direct node check; no tracked source file uses either form (crlf-count=0, no carrier holds /* inside a string), so the recorded phase state stays true and the fixture stays exact. The phase overall is not closable on my pass alone.
